title: The Honolulu Symphony and filling in for Sarah Vaughan
summary: After three years in Honolulu he subbed with Vaughan at Sardi's and Joe Glaser called him crazy for turning down Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: The Honolulu Symphony. Barati was the conductor. So anyhow, after spending three years over there, I came back, and one night at Sardi's... Do you remember Sardi's?

Sarah Vaughan's bass player was in an automobile accident or something, and I got a last-minute call from I guess, Ronnell Bright (I think he was working with her), to come and fill in. So I go play with her. And in the audience later is Joe Glaser. So he saw me up there, and he said, 'There's that crazy son-of-a-bitch. I can't pay him to... He's crazy. I tried to make him famous, and he turned me down.' So I guess he thought I was a nut. But I've always felt like if they want me, well, give me some money. Everybody's making something, give me some, too! So I've never gotten rich, but at least I've been happy.
